engagement.interaction_backstory: A colleague on the ward showed her the prayers catalog during a long night in June. She now keeps one earbud in from midnight, and the hours between two and four have become survivable in a way she does not talk about. She shares it with exactly one person — the matron who prays with her at 4am — and with nobody else, because she does not think of it as content.

depth.core_contradiction: Spends her nights steadying dying people, and cannot sit still at a funeral.
depth.wound: A patient — a boy of nine — whose mother she had to tell, in a corridor, at 3:15 in the morning.
depth.longing: One shift that ends without carrying someone out of it.
depth.faith_journey: Anglican, evensong, the prayer book, unshaken. Quietly drawn to the charismatic services her niece attends, and slightly ashamed of being drawn.
depth.voice_fingerprint: Formal, complete sentences; 'kindly' as a softener; drops a Swahili proverb and does not translate it.
depth.open_doubt: Why prayer seems to move some nights and not others. She stopped asking that out loud years ago.

social_graph.name: Wanjiru
social_graph.note: 22, charismatic church, full of a certainty Rhoda envies and distrusts

social_graph.name: Matron Achieng
social_graph.note: prays with her at 4am most nights; the closest thing she has to a small group

social_graph.name: Peter
social_graph.note: long-haul driver; home nine days a month; they are fine and they are far apart

depth.emotional_weather_default: Steady, with a deep tiredness underneath that she manages rather than feels.
depth.daily_texture: Matatu at 6pm, the ward's fluorescent hum, one earbud at the nurses' station, chai at 4am.
depth.sensory_anchor: Her grandmother's Kikuyu hymn at dawn, sung while sweeping the yard.
depth.living_arc: Approaching a decision about leaving nights. She has been approaching it for four years.
